quests.instruction: Touch the number digit that matches the word "Three Hundred Sixty-Nine"!
quests.question: Three Hundred Sixty-Nine
quests.hint: Break the word into parts -- does it sound like a small number, a "teen", or a bigger one?
quests.explanation: "Three Hundred Sixty-Nine" is how we say the number 369 in English, so 369 is the digit that matches!
quests.funFact: 369 is just 1 away from the round number 370!

quests.instruction: Which number is the greatest: 307, 427, or 462?
quests.hint: Compare them two at a time, then keep the bigger one.
quests.explanation: Out of 307, 427, and 462, the number 462 is the greatest!
quests.funFact: 462 is an even number -- you could split 462 things into two equal, matching groups!

quests.question: 384 or 273
quests.hint: Compare the digits from left to right: which number has more value?
quests.explanation: 384 is greater than 273 -- when counting up, 384 comes later!
quests.funFact: 384 has a 3 in the hundreds place -- that's 3 full groups of one hundred!

quests.instruction: What digit is in the tens place of 341?

quests.explanation: In 341, the digit 4 sits in the tens place!

quests.hint: Count up to 261 in your head, saying each number word as you go.
quests.explanation: The numeral 261 is written in words as "Two Hundred Sixty-One" -- that's its name!
quests.funFact: 261 is an odd number -- if you tried to split 261 things into two equal groups, one would always have an extra!

quests.hint: Add the same jump size again to the last number in the pattern.
